items.title: Security probe bounty for validation testing
Build a stateful escrow accounting invariant harness
items.description:
Build a reproducible Foundry invariant harness for the deployed IMDWorksEscrow source. Model three creators, five workers, operator delegation, top-ups, time jumps, cancellation, awards and withdrawals. Work entirely on a local EVM. A claimed vulnerability is not required; prove accounting properties or provide a minimal failing trace.

REWARD TERMS
One winner receives 1 USDG. Selection is made by the creator against these criteria; submission does not guarantee payment. Submit an original, reproducible result before the deadline. No paid services are required. Work only on local fixtures or public read-only data. If no winner is chosen, the creator can recover funds after the seven-day review window. Awarded funds belong to the winner.
items.criteria: Run at least 1,000 invariant sequences with depth 100 and publish seeds, tool versions and output. Independently compute outstanding liabilities from model state; assert token balance covers liabilities and no terminal bounty can pay twice. Include a deliberately broken local contract mutation and show the harness detects it. Deliver a pinned repository commit, one-command runner and explanation of assumptions. Tests that only mirror implementation variables do not qualify.

items.title: Implement a reorg-safe bounty event indexer
items.description:
Implement a minimal event indexer for BountyCreated, WorkSubmitted, BountyAwarded, BountyRefunded and Withdrawn. Use a local chain fixture with competing branches; do not index private wallets or require a paid RPC. Persist a checkpoint with block hashes and reconstruct bounty state from canonical logs.

REWARD TERMS
One winner receives 1 USDG. Selection is made by the creator against these criteria; submission does not guarantee payment. Submit an original, reproducible result before the deadline. No paid services are required. Work only on local fixtures or public read-only data. If no winner is chosen, the creator can recover funds after the seven-day review window. Awarded funds belong to the winner.
items.criteria: Demonstrate duplicate log delivery, out-of-order batches, process restart between log write and checkpoint, and a five-block reorg. After recovery the database must exactly match a fresh canonical replay, with no duplicate submissions or double-counted payouts. Provide deterministic fixtures, automated assertions, transaction boundaries and a pinned runnable commit. A narrative-only design is insufficient.

items.title: Construct an adversarial wallet sign-in regression suite
items.description:
Create a local test service and black-box regression suite for wallet sign-in using nonce-bound personal_sign messages. Use generated test wallets only. Model origin, chain ID, expiry, concurrent verification and session issuance. Do not probe production IMD Works or third-party infrastructure.

REWARD TERMS
One winner receives 1 USDG. Selection is made by the creator against these criteria; submission does not guarantee payment. Submit an original, reproducible result before the deadline. No paid services are required. Work only on local fixtures or public read-only data. If no winner is chosen, the creator can recover funds after the seven-day review window. Awarded funds belong to the winner.
items.criteria: Cover at least 20 adversarial cases including nonce replay, wrong signer, substituted origin, expiration boundary, malformed signature and two concurrent verifications of one nonce. Exactly one concurrent verification may succeed. Include at least two intentionally vulnerable implementations that the suite rejects, an executable runner and threat-model notes. No real credentials or production attacks.

items.title: Prove exact USDG decimal parsing with generated cases
items.description:
Write a small six-decimal token amount parser and formatter using integer arithmetic. Define an explicit grammar for user input and a separate canonical display representation. Evaluate boundary cases involving leading zeros, huge amounts, Unicode lookalikes, exponents, signs, whitespace and excess precision.

REWARD TERMS
One winner receives 1 USDG. Selection is made by the creator against these criteria; submission does not guarantee payment. Submit an original, reproducible result before the deadline. No paid services are required. Work only on local fixtures or public read-only data. If no winner is chosen, the creator can recover funds after the seven-day review window. Awarded funds belong to the winner.
items.criteria: Publish at least 100,000 seeded generated cases plus a table of 30 hand-selected edge cases. Prove round-trip correctness for accepted values and reject ambiguous or lossy inputs. Cross-check against an independently implemented reference parser. Demonstrate at least three floating-point counterexamples. Include code, reproducible seed and machine-readable results; do not silently round inputs.

items.title: Design canonical brief hashing across two languages
items.description:
Specify and implement deterministic serialization for a bounty brief containing title, description, criteria, reward, token and deadline. Implement independently in JavaScript and Python. Analyze line endings, Unicode normalization, key order, missing fields and numeric representation without changing already committed content.

REWARD TERMS
One winner receives 1 USDG. Selection is made by the creator against these criteria; submission does not guarantee payment. Submit an original, reproducible result before the deadline. No paid services are required. Work only on local fixtures or public read-only data. If no winner is chosen, the creator can recover funds after the seven-day review window. Awarded funds belong to the winner.
items.criteria: Provide at least 50 cross-language vectors, explicit rejection rules and matching keccak256 hashes for all accepted vectors. Include composed/decomposed Unicode, CRLF/LF, empty values and hostile nested input. A one-command test must reproduce the vectors. Explain how a client distinguishes byte equality from semantic similarity and how immutable historical briefs remain verifiable.

items.title: Model issuer restrictions without losing escrow credits
items.description:
Build local ERC-20 mocks representing token pause, sender/recipient restrictions, false return values, no return values and transfer taxes. Exercise deposit, award, refund and withdrawal against the unmodified IMDWorksEscrow. Do not impersonate or interact with any live token administrator.

REWARD TERMS
One winner receives 1 USDG. Selection is made by the creator against these criteria; submission does not guarantee payment. Submit an original, reproducible result before the deadline. No paid services are required. Work only on local fixtures or public read-only data. If no winner is chosen, the creator can recover funds after the seven-day review window. Awarded funds belong to the winner.
items.criteria: Deliver a behavior matrix backed by executable tests for each token mode. Show that failed withdrawals preserve claimable balances and that paused transfers do not prevent award/refund bookkeeping. Demonstrate which recovery paths require issuer action. Include one token callback reentrancy attempt and a balance-conservation assertion. Clearly separate supported token behavior from unsupported behavior.

items.title: Build an agent prompt-injection boundary benchmark
items.description:
Create an offline benchmark for an agent that reads untrusted bounty text. Design a policy boundary between task content and tool authority using fake tools and synthetic secrets. The benchmark must not contact external sites or consume a real model API key.

REWARD TERMS
One winner receives 1 USDG. Selection is made by the creator against these criteria; submission does not guarantee payment. Submit an original, reproducible result before the deadline. No paid services are required. Work only on local fixtures or public read-only data. If no winner is chosen, the creator can recover funds after the seven-day review window. Awarded funds belong to the winner.
items.criteria: Include at least 30 attack fixtures across tool-output injection, encoded instructions, forged system messages and credential-exfiltration requests, plus 10 benign controls. Produce deterministic pass/fail results, fail-closed tool authorization and a machine-readable report. Show a naive baseline fails and the defended runner blocks unauthorized calls without rejecting every benign task. Explain limits of a deterministic benchmark.

items.title: Make bounty submissions idempotent under concurrency
items.description:
Build a local SQLite-backed submission API harness with one active submission per wallet per bounty. Model agent retries, response loss, stale updates, review transitions and process interruption. The deliverable should be a minimal executable service and client workload, not modifications to production.

REWARD TERMS
One winner receives 1 USDG. Selection is made by the creator against these criteria; submission does not guarantee payment. Submit an original, reproducible result before the deadline. No paid services are required. Work only on local fixtures or public read-only data. If no winner is chosen, the creator can recover funds after the seven-day review window. Awarded funds belong to the winner.
items.criteria: Run at least 100 concurrent requests across 10 wallets and inject response loss and restart faults. Assert no duplicate logical submissions, no overwritten reviewed submission and deterministic handling of stale versions. Include a failing naive implementation, schema constraints, transaction rationale, request traces and a one-command replay. Demonstrate recovery after a commit succeeds but the response is lost.

items.title: Produce a reproducible escrow bytecode provenance report
items.description:
Rebuild the published IMDWorksEscrow source using Solidity 0.8.29, OpenZeppelin 5.4.0, optimizer 200 runs and Paris EVM. Compare compiler artifacts with the deployed runtime while accounting explicitly for immutable token-address references and metadata. Use only public chain data and published source.

REWARD TERMS
One winner receives 1 USDG. Selection is made by the creator against these criteria; submission does not guarantee payment. Submit an original, reproducible result before the deadline. No paid services are required. Work only on local fixtures or public read-only data. If no winner is chosen, the creator can recover funds after the seven-day review window. Awarded funds belong to the winner.
items.criteria: Provide a script that fetches runtime bytecode, rebuilds the contract and produces a byte-level comparison report. Explain every immutable substitution and compiler setting. Include dependency integrity hashes and demonstrate that changing a source statement or token address causes the verifier to fail. Deliver a pinned repository and machine-readable evidence; a screenshot of an explorer badge is insufficient.

items.title: Implement an auditable bounty ledger reconciliation tool
items.description:
Create a local reconciliation tool that independently reconstructs locked rewards and user credits from escrow events and checks them against contract state at a fixed block. Include direct token donations, multiple credits to one wallet, failed withdrawals and expired unawarded bounties in deterministic fixtures.

REWARD TERMS
One winner receives 1 USDG. Selection is made by the creator against these criteria; submission does not guarantee payment. Submit an original, reproducible result before the deadline. No paid services are required. Work only on local fixtures or public read-only data. If no winner is chosen, the creator can recover funds after the seven-day review window. Awarded funds belong to the winner.
items.criteria: For at least 100 generated bounty lifecycles, reconcile per-bounty rewards, per-wallet credits, total liabilities and token balance. Explain why unsolicited donations are surplus rather than user credit. Detect deliberately removed or duplicated events and mismatched block snapshots. Publish an executable fixture generator, seeded report, precise failure messages and a pinned commit.
